intro: Lo que, el que and lo + adjective: three tools for making longer sentences.
p.lo que.consejo: It speaks of an idea or something unnamed: «lo que dices». In a question you use «qué».
p.el que.consejo: It replaces a masculine noun already mentioned: «el libro» → «el que quiero».
p.la que.consejo: It agrees with the noun: «la chica con la que hablé». After a preposition, the article comes before «que».
p.los que.consejo: It names a group without saying who: «los que llegan tarde». If all are women, «las que».
p.lo bueno.consejo: «Lo» + adjective names a quality as an idea: «lo bueno», «lo malo». «Lo» never changes.
p.lo malo.consejo: It is usually followed by «es que»: «Lo malo es que…» introduces the problem.
p.lo importante.consejo: The stress is on «TAN». «Es» and an infinitive or «que» usually follow: «lo importante es que…».
p.lo mejor.consejo: «Mejor» already means «more good»: you say «lo mejor», never «lo más mejor».
p.lo mismo.consejo: It is a fixed phrase: «quiero lo mismo». With a noun, «mismo» does change: «la misma».
p.todo lo que.consejo: «Todo» goes before «lo que»: «todo lo que dices». The phrase never changes.
p.la razón por la que.consejo: It agrees with «razón», which is feminine. With «motivo» you say «el motivo por el que».
p.quiere decir.consejo: «Querer decir» means «to mean»; it is not about wanting: «¿Qué quiere decir esta palabra?».
b1.titulo: What, the one who, the good thing
b1.texto:
**Lo que** speaks of an idea or of something without a name: **lo que** quiero es descansar. When you ask, you use **qué**: ¿Qué quieres?

**El que, la que, los que, las que** replace a noun already mentioned and agree with it: este libro es **el que** quiero; **los que** llegan tarde no entran.

**Lo + adjective** names an idea: **lo bueno**, **lo malo**, **lo importante**. It often goes with **es que**: **Lo bueno es que** es barato.
b2.f0.texto: I do not understand what this email says.
b2.f1.texto: What it means is that there is a meeting tomorrow.
b2.f2.texto: What about those who cannot go?
b2.f3.texto: The good thing is that you can watch it from home.
b2.f4.texto: The bad thing is that it starts at eight in the morning.
b2.f5.texto: That is the reason why I am not going.
b2.f6.texto: Then I will tell you everything they say.
b2.f7.texto: The best thing is to sleep a little more.
b4.titulo: With a preposition and without one
b4.texto:
With a preposition, the article goes before **que** and agrees with the noun:

- la chica **con la que** hablé
- el día **en el que** nací
- la razón **por la que** no voy

**Lo que** never changes, neither in gender nor in number: **todo lo que** dices, **lo que** quiero.

And **lo** + adjective does not change either: **lo importante** es llegar a tiempo.
b4.e1.texto: The girl I spoke with works here.
b4.e2.texto: The important thing is to arrive on time.
b5.f0.texto: Lucía reads the email in the silent room under the yellow light of the lamp.
b5.f1.texto: The words she sees first are written in big black letters.
b5.f2.texto: What the email says sounds serious and distant, like a voice without a face.
b5.f3.texto: Outside, the rain taps the windowpanes with a soft, steady noise.
b5.f4.texto: Lucía breathes deeply and rereads calmly what she has not understood.
b5.f5.texto: Pablo comes in with two cups of steaming tea and sits down beside her.
b5.f6.texto: The one she prefers smells of cinnamon and orange.
b5.f7.texto: The two of them quietly read the lines that talk about the meeting.
b5.f8.texto: Little by little, what looked like a problem becomes a simple appointment.
b5.f9.texto: Then the room fills again with a warm calm, like the air of a summer afternoon.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! With no noun before it, you use «lo que».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «El que» replaces a masculine noun and there is none here.
b6.pregunta: It speaks of an idea. Which words are missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: That is it! «Lo» + adjective names an idea and never changes.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «El bueno» is a specific person or thing, «the good one».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «La buena» is a specific woman or feminine thing, not an idea.
b7.pregunta: How do you say «the good thing»?
b8.frase: Todo lo que dices es verdad
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Lo que» does not agree: it is for ideas, not for «chica».
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «Con la que» agrees with «chica», which is feminine.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «El que» is masculine and «chica» is feminine.
b9.pregunta: «Chica» is feminine. Which article goes with «que»?
b10.o0.refuerzo: No: «los que llegan tarde» does not include the punctual ones.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Los» is plural: it speaks of several people.
b10.o2.refuerzo: That is it! «Los que» names a group without saying who it is.
b10.pregunta: «Los que llegan tarde no entran.» Who does not go in?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «The good thing is that it is cheap».
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Lo importante» names an idea, not a specific thing.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «El importante» needs a specific masculine noun.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «La importante» needs a specific feminine noun.
b12.pregunta: There is no noun. What goes before «importante»?
p.pueden.consejo: Plural of «puede», from «poder». Use it for several people: «ellos pueden».
p.silenciosa.consejo: From «silencio». The «ci» sounds like «th» in Spain, so say «si-len-THYO-sa».
p.escritas.consejo: Past participle of «escribir». It agrees with the feminine noun «letras»: «escritas».
p.rostro.consejo: Sounds like «rrostro» at the start. Think of a «rostro» as the face you see.
p.relee.consejo: From «releer», «leer» again. The two «e» vowels sit in separate syllables: «le-e».
p.entendido.consejo: Past participle of «entender». With «no ha» it means «has not understood».
p.humeante.consejo: From «humo», smoke. The «h» is silent, so say «oo-me-AN-te».
p.parecía.consejo: Imperfect of «parecer». The accent on «í» is the stress: «pa-re-THI-a».
p.convierte.consejo: From «convertir». The «v» sounds like «b» in Spanish, and «ie» is one stressed sound.
